claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you some questions.

Let me start with a few basic questions:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi, yes I have one child - my son Alex. He's 17 and lives at home with me. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I can help you determine if you're eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.

Let me ask you some questions to assess your eligibility:

**Is Alex currently in full-time non-advanced education or approved training?** (For example, is he studying for A-levels, Scottish Highers, or similar qualifications at school or college?)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not in school or college anymore. He's actually started an apprenticeship - he's training to be an electrician.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Apprenticeships can be considered approved training for Child Benefit purposes.

**Is Alex's apprenticeship an approved training program, and did he start it before his 18th birthday?** (Most apprenticeships registered with the relevant authorities are considered approved training)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, it's a proper registered apprenticeship program, and he started it a few months ago, so well before he turns 18.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. 

**When exactly does Alex turn 18?** (I need to know his date of birth or when his 18th birthday will be)

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He'll be turning 18 in about 5 months' time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing that information. Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment:

**Are you the person responsible for Alex - meaning, do you live with him and are you responsible for his care and upbringing?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. He lives here at home with me and I'm responsible for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. One final question:

**Are you currently living in the UK, and is Alex also living in the UK with you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, we both live in the UK - we're in Manchester.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**Good news! You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Based on the information you've provided:

- Alex is 17 years old and in a registered apprenticeship that he started before turning 18
- He lives with you in the UK and you're responsible for him
- Approved training programs (including registered apprenticeships) qualify for Child Benefit

**You can claim Child Benefit for Alex until he turns 18.** Child Benefit will continue until the week containing his 18th birthday, which is in approximately 5 months' time.

**Important to note:** Once Alex turns 18, Child Benefit will stop, even though he's still in his apprenticeship. After age 18, only full-time non-advanced education (like A-levels or similar qualifications) qualifies for Child Benefit - apprenticeships do not qualify beyond the 18th birthday.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit now and potentially receive backdated payments (up to 3 months). If you have any questions about making a claim, please let me know!
